title: Nanobubble nucleation and growth dynamics in the presence of gold nanoparticles observed by liquid transmission electron microscopy
content: Electron beam-induced nanobubbles (NBs) are an intrinsic feature of liquid transmission electron microscopy experiments, yet their evolution in the presence of nanoparticles (NPs) remains poorly understood. This work investigates the nucleation, growth, and area coverage of electron beam-induced NBs in aqueous environments with and without Au NPs in the field of view. In NP-free regions, small numbers of NBs grow rapidly and reach large diameters, leading to steadily increasing NB area coverage over time. In contrast, NBs generated in the presence of NPs exhibit enhanced nucleation, producing a large number of small, early-stage bubbles. As irradiation continues, NB growth in the presence of NPs is suppressed. Quantitative analysis suggests that beam-induced NBs in these experiments are surface NBs with higher curvature than those reported in prior literature. Enhanced early-stage growth of NBs in the presence of NPs is attributed to chemical mechanisms, namely Au NP-catalyzed hydrogen evolution reactions. Late-stage, impeded growth of NBs in the presence of NPs is attributed to Au NP-catalyzed oxygen evolution reactions reducing local H2 gas saturation, and physical interactions between NPs and NBs constraining bubble lateral growth. The results provide new insight into the effects of localized environment on beam-induced NB nucleation and growth.
